paragraphs.text: Bamboo is sometimes promoted as an ideal sustainable material. Some species can grow almost a metre in a single day, and the plant regrows from its roots after cutting, so it does not need to be replanted. Its strength-to-weight ratio is comparable to that of steel, which is why it has been used for scaffolding in Asia for centuries. However, turning bamboo into textiles often involves toxic chemicals, and plantations sometimes replace natural forests, reducing their environmental benefits.
